text:
Closing as already delivered by e72cb51 (2026-09-09, "Give signed data a colour
primitive, and measure what a reader can separate"), which no commit message
cited, so this bead stayed open after the work landed. Each request against
main at c106b87:

1. Diverging constructor with negative/neutral/positive on a symmetric domain,
   raster and scene forms: `DivergingPalette` in Color.scala, where -1 is the
   negative endpoint, 0 is exactly the neutral and +1 the positive, and `pixel`
   is `color` packed, so an overlay and a scene mark of one value cannot
   disagree. `DivergingColorizer` carries a magnitude and `ContinuousScale.diverging`
   fixes the symmetric domain, so the library owns the midpoint on both paths.
2. Oklab interpolation: `Oklab` with `mix`; each arm of the palette interpolates
   through it rather than through sRGB bytes.
3. Named colour-vision-safe default: `DivergingPalette.BlueRust`, alongside
   `ColorVision` (Brettel, Vienot & Mollon 1997) and `ColorSeparation` for CIE76
   distance as a named observer sees it.
4. docs/accessibility.md: sequential versus diverging guidance at lines 50-77,
   and "Rainbow and jet are refused" at line 169.

The "worth considering alongside" categorical gap was answered in the same
commit: the default theme palette moved to the first six Okabe-Ito colours, and
`AccessibilityDiagnostic.IndistinguishablePalette` reports a discrete scale
whose closest pair falls under `ColorSeparation.SeriesFloor`, naming observer
and levels.

Not what closes this: `ScalarScale.diverging`, added today in #6, is a generic
two-ramp scale about an explicit centre for `ScalarMapping`, with no neutral
guarantee and no perceptual claim. It does not supersede `DivergingPalette`.
